mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 3 Series M340d engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for a BMW M340d costs £2,500-£9,000 depending on condition and specification. Used B57D30B engines start from £2,500, reconditioned units range from £4,500-£7,000, and fully rebuilt engines with warranty cost £5,500-£8,500. Fitting adds £800-£1,500 due to the engine's complexity and 48V mild-hybrid system.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of engine problems in a BMW M340d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common symptoms include DPF warning lights, reduced performance (limp mode), rough idling, increased fuel consumption, rattling from the engine bay (wastegate actuator), and coolant loss without visible leaks.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 3 Series M340d?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical M340d is worth £30,000-£55,000 depending on age and mileage. A rebuilt engine at £5,500-£8,500 is well within the vehicle's value. However, the B57 engine is fundamentally robust - most owners will never need a full engine replacement. Targeted repairs (DPF cleaning, coolant pipe replacement, wastegate actuator) are usually the right answer.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 3 Series M340d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical engine replacement takes 3-5 days for a specialist due to the 48V mild-hybrid system complexity - including removal of the old unit, HV system isolation, fitting the replacement, and testing. Some suppliers offer delivery on used engines, but fitting always requires workshop time.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the B57D30B and B57D30T2 engines in the M340d?

acceptedAnswer.text: Both engines produce 340 hp and 700 Nm of torque. The B57D30B was fitted from 2020-2024, while the B57D30T2 (2023-present) features updated emissions hardware to comply with Euro 6e standards. Performance is identical; the T2 variant is primarily an emissions update.

mainEntity.name: Does a rebuilt BMW M340d engine come with a warranty?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket carries a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. This covers manufacturing defects and component failure, giving you peace of mind. Always confirm exact warranty terms with your chosen supplier before purchase.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 3 Series M340d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW M340d debuted in 2020 as the first M Performance diesel in the 3 Series range, positioned between the 330d and the full-fat M3. Powered by the B57D30B 3.0-litre straight-six diesel with twin turbochargers and 48V mild-hybrid technology, the M340d produces 340 hp and a monumental 700 Nm of torque - making it one of the most potent production diesel saloons ever built.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 3 Series M340d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The BMW M340d is powered by the B57D30B 3.0-litre twin-turbo diesel - a highly sophisticated engine that delivers effortless performance. However, modern diesel emissions systems introduce complexity, and the M340d's high-performance nature means components are subjected to significant stress. Rebuilt units supplied through our network include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: DPF & EGR System Clogging - Why the BMW 3 Series M340d Needs Regular Motorway Runs
problems.rootCause: The Diesel Particulate Filter (DPF) traps soot from exhaust gases and requires regular regeneration - achieved by sustained motorway driving at 40 mph or above. Short journeys prevent the DPF from reaching regeneration temperature, leading to clogging. The EGR valve and cooler also accumulate carbon deposits, causing rough idling, reduced performance and increased fuel consumption.

repairOptions.longevity: First step if DPF warning light appears

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove, clean and refit DPF; clean EGR valve and cooler
repairOptions.longevity: If forced regen fails; restores performance
Only in catastrophic cases - extremely rare on B57

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series M340d is worth £30,000-£55,000 depending on age, mileage and specification. Full engine replacement at £5,500-£8,500 is well within the vehicle's value, but most M340d owners will never need one - the B57 engine is fundamentally robust when properly maintained.
problems.recommendation: If you primarily use your M340d for short urban trips, take it for a 30-minute motorway run every 2-3 weeks to allow the DPF to regenerate. Regular oil changes (every 10,000 miles rather than BMW's 15,500-mile interval) are strongly recommended to prevent sludge buildup that can affect the EGR and turbo systems.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt B57D30B BMW 3 Series M340d engine prices

problems.h4: Coolant System Leaks - Why the BMW 3 Series M340d Loses Coolant
problems.rootCause: A known coolant pipe on the passenger side of the engine towards the front is prone to cracking and leaking. The pipe sits under the intake manifold, making it difficult to spot without specialist inspection. Water pump failure is also reported, though less common than the pipe issue.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked pipe, flush and refill coolant

repairOptions.longevity: If water pump is the source of the leak
Only if overheating has caused internal damage - very rare

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series M340d is worth £30,000-£55,000. A coolant pipe replacement at £500-£900 is a fraction of the vehicle's value and should be carried out promptly if coolant loss is detected.
problems.recommendation: Check your coolant level regularly - if you see the low coolant warning, have the system pressure tested immediately. The known pipe failure is well-documented by specialists and is repairable without engine removal. Don't ignore coolant loss - overheating can lead to head gasket failure and, in extreme cases, require a full engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare coolant system repair quotes for your M340d

problems.h4: Turbocharger Wastegate Actuator Wear - Why the BMW 3 Series M340d Loses Boost
problems.rootCause: The twin-turbo setup uses wastegate actuators to regulate boost pressure. Over time, the actuator can wear out or become stuck, leading to loss of boost pressure, reduced engine performance, and a rattling noise from the engine at low speeds or idle.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty actuator, recalibrate boost control
repairOptions.longevity: Cost-effective if caught early; restores full power
If wastegate failure has damaged the turbo
Only in catastrophic turbo failure cases

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical BMW 3 Series M340d is worth £30,000-£55,000. Wastegate actuator replacement at £700-£1,200 is a manageable repair for a car of this value.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine bay at low speeds or experience a noticeable drop in power, have the turbocharger system inspected immediately. Replacing a faulty wastegate actuator costs significantly less than a full turbocharger or engine replacement.
